instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Regional public health authority responsible for epidemiological surveillance, health promotion programs, and healthcare resource planning for a region of 1.2 million inhabitants. Managing 15 public health programs. Key innovation priority is real-time disease surveillance using syndromic data integration from primary care and hospital networks. The company has mature core business processes but struggles with the tension between running the existing operation efficiently and carving out resources for innovation. We have pockets of digital maturity in specific teams while other areas rely heavily on manual workflows and spreadsheets.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: Our board has set an ambitious revenue target of reaching €50M ARR within 5 years from our current base. This requires us to expand our addressable market, potentially pivot pricing models from one-time to recurring revenue, and build a repeatable enterprise sales motion. We need to identify the highest-leverage growth levers without overextending our cash runway.
answers.teamSize: Our R&D function consists of 10-12 engineers organized into two squads: one focused on core product innovation and one on exploratory/new business model prototyping. We also have 2 dedicated data engineers building our analytics infrastructure. Innovation projects follow a lean startup methodology with clear go/no-go criteria at 3-month checkpoints.

input.changes_since_last: Transitioning from founder-led to professional management. Hired 3 senior leaders. Strategic planning process being formalized.

opportunities.title: Establishing a Federated Data Interoperability Layer for Surveillance (Carry Forward)
opportunities.rationale: The core mission relies on integrating diverse, siloed data sources from primary care and hospitals. To achieve real-time surveillance at scale in a high regulatory environment, the technical focus must shift from collecting isolated datasets to building governed access layers that ensure compliance while facilitating predictive analytics. This layer is critical for achieving the highest growth impact.

first_actions: Draft necessary Data Sharing Agreements (DSAs) and legal frameworks with key hospital networks, prioritizing GDPR/HIPAA compliance steps.
Develop a conceptual data model defining standardized APIs and identity resolution protocols across participating systems.
Conduct pilot feasibility studies on connecting two non-critical adjacent data sources (e.g., lab results to primary care records) to test interoperability limits.
resources_needed: Legal counsel specializing in public health/data governance
Cloud infrastructure budget for secure sandbox environment
execution_plan.success_metric: Number of signed MOUs with critical data partners and operational proof-of-concept connecting 3 distinct systems.
milestones: Completion of internal gap analysis for current data APIs (Q1)
Signature of initial DSA with the largest partner hospital network (Q2)
Launch of minimal viable interoperability layer connecting two sources in a secure sandbox (Q3)

opportunities.title: Structured Market Validation Framework for Digital Products (Carry Forward)
opportunities.rationale: The past MVP failure indicates that technical execution is not enough; there is a systemic gap in validating market need before building. This opportunity shifts the focus from 'building' to rigorous, structured discovery using rapid user interviews and value chain mapping to identify high-leverage recurring revenue streams.

first_actions: Formalize a 'Discovery Sprint' process requiring executive sign-off before any solution design begins.
Implement mandatory value stream mapping workshops involving sales, clinical operations, and finance to identify points of friction that can be productized.
Develop structured interview scripts targeting pain points rather than desired features from potential paying clients.
Conduct regulatory compliance review with legal team to ensure alignment with applicable regulations
resources_needed: 20% time allocation from senior leadership for stakeholder interviews
Small budget for participation in external user groups
execution_plan.success_metric: Creation of a prioritized backlog of 3 validated, market-ready use cases with clear willingness-to-pay estimates.
milestones: Completion of mapping critical operational value chains (Q1)
Running 5 structured discovery sprints focused on different user segments (Q2)
Presentation to the board detailing the top 3 prioritized product hypotheses and estimated ROI.

next_steps.action: Establish a dedicated cross-functional Governance Board (Legal, Tech, Operations) responsible for overseeing all data sharing agreements and regulatory compliance before any development begins.
Define the Minimum Viable Go-to-Market (MVGM) process: mapping the journey from identified pain point to contracted recurring revenue, ensuring sales and product teams are aligned.
Institute mandatory 'Pre-Mortem' reviews for all new initiatives, forcing the team to identify potential failure points (regulatory, technical, adoption) before resource allocation.

key_weaknesses: Structural tension between maintaining efficient core operations and dedicating resources to speculative innovation.
Lack of established, rigorous market validation processes for defining commercial product scope (evidenced by MVP failure).
Over-reliance on complex technical solutions without sufficient pre-work on regulatory/legal data governance.

improvements: Formalization of the strategic planning process and professional leadership structure in place.
Dedicated R&D capacity (two squads) has been successfully allocated for structured innovation sprints.
Increased focus on technical capability, demonstrated by building an initial MVP prototype.
persistent_gaps: The organization still struggles to allocate resources from existing operational demands towards growth initiatives without executive mandate or dedicated funding streams.
Translating technical feasibility (building the platform) into commercial viability (selling the solution) remains a significant bottleneck.
Data governance maturity lags behind technical capability, posing risks in high-regulation contexts.
achieved_milestones: Successful hiring and integration of senior professional leadership.
Operationalizing the lean startup methodology with fixed 3-month checkpoints for new initiatives.
Completion of the initial MVP prototype buildout (though validation failed).

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: Significant shift from founder-led ambiguity to professional management structure. Process formalization and dedicated R&D teams have been established. Focus has intensified on commercializing growth levers rather than just technical capability.
